Export a NICHESObject to TissuePlex edges.parquet

Source: R/export_to_TissuePlex.R
export_to_TissuePlex.Rd

Writes a Parquet file that TissuePlex can load directly as its edge layer. Every edge in $edge.list is exported. Edges present in $edge.data produce one row per (edge, LRM) pair with real scores; edges absent from $edge.data (no active LR signal) produce a single placeholder row with NA for all LRM fields. This ensures TissuePlex can render the full tissue graph even for edges with no scored LR pairs.

Usage

export_to_TissuePlex(
  object,
  output.path,
  x.col = "x",
  y.col = "y",
  celltype.col = "celltype",
  n.threads = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A NICHESObject.

output.path

Full path to the output .parquet file. Parent directories are created automatically.

x.col

Name of the x-coordinate column in $cell.meta (default "x").

y.col

Name of the y-coordinate column in $cell.meta (default "y").

celltype.col

Name of the cell-type column in $cell.meta, or NULL to omit cell-type columns (default "celltype").

n.threads

Number of threads for data.table operations (NULL uses the current getDTthreads() setting). On a MacBook Pro, setting this to the number of performance cores (e.g. 8–12) significantly speeds up joins and string operations on large datasets.

Value

Invisibly returns output.path.

Details

NICHESv2 stops at this file. To view it, see the TissuePlex manual.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("arrow", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(NICHESv2_example)
  out.file <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
  export_to_TissuePlex(NICHESv2_example, output.path = out.file)
  unlink(out.file)
}
#> Wrote 403 rows | 141 scored edges (15 LRMs) | 213 unscored edges -> /tmp/RtmpZzMH1L/file2141b7991a8.parquet
